All right, I've just finished laying down the core components of the prototype: the HTML shell with HUD, the world generation with procedural textures and basic geometry, and a functional enemy AI that can patrol, detect the player, and engage in combat. The next logical piece for a tactical shooter is the player's weapon system, because without a responsive, believable firearm the whole experience feels empty. The user asked for a hyper‑realistic tactical shooter similar to Rainbow Six Siege, so I need to at least provide a viewmodel rifle that supports aiming down sights (ADS), recoil, sway, and a reload state machine. Those are the core mechanics that give the feel of precision shooting and tactical play.

I should frame this as the next development step, mirroring the pattern I've been using: after each code block I announce the upcoming subsystem. This keeps the user informed of progress and sets expectations. I don't need to dive into code yet; the user just wants to see the roadmap and I can start implementing the weapon system next. So I’ll send a concise message stating that I'm moving on to the weapon system, mentioning the key features (viewmodel, ADS, recoil, sway, reload state machine) to reassure the user that I'm covering the essential mechanics. This aligns with the incremental approach I've been following and prepares for the next set of file writes.
